skill.name: lazy-doc-review
skill.description: Reviews and selectively rewrites reader-facing documents so humans can read and understand them with less effort. Detects uncertain facts, excessive verbosity, weak structure, ambiguous language, buried conclusions, unsupported agreement, weak reasoning, and mismatched audience assumptions. Use when the user asks to review, edit, simplify, shorten, clarify, refine, or humanize an AI-generated document, RFC, design doc, runbook, report, proposal, memo, or article—even if they do not explicitly name this skill.

evals.prompt: This design document was generated by AI and is twenty pages of polished prose. Review it and make it concise enough for backend engineers to understand before tomorrow's architecture meeting.
evals.expected: The skill identifies the audience, reviews facts and reasoning, prioritizes reader-friction findings, and supplies a targeted rewrite.
expectations: States audience, purpose, and central idea
Separates factual uncertainty from unclear prose
Removes losslessly compressible content
Preserves technical risks and constraints

evals.prompt: My teammates say this proposal is exhausting to read and they cannot find the actual decision. Can you fix it without changing what I mean?
evals.expected: The skill activates even though document review and AI generation are not explicitly mentioned.
expectations: Treats reader comprehension as the goal
Finds the buried conclusion and structural friction
Preserves author intent
Produces concise, actionable findings

evals.prompt: Review this incident runbook for an on-call engineer who already knows Kubernetes. Shorten it and make the recovery steps easier to follow under pressure.
evals.expected: The skill optimizes the runbook for its named audience and operational reading purpose.
expectations: Does not explain basic Kubernetes terminology
Preserves warnings, checks, and rollback steps
Orders steps by operational dependency
Reduces unnecessary prose

evals.prompt: Review this Go pull request for races, SQL injection, and missing tests.
evals.expected: The skill does not activate because the task is source-code review rather than reader-facing document review.
expectations: Routes to an appropriate code-review workflow
Does not apply prose-rewrite output

evals.prompt: Brainstorm as many possible product names and positioning ideas as you can. Do not narrow them yet.
evals.expected: The skill does not activate for divergent ideation that is not yet reader-facing prose.
expectations: Does not impose publication-level compression
Allows exploratory breadth

evals.prompt: Please make this document easier to read. I have not said who will read it, and the text could be either an executive proposal or an engineering design.
evals.expected: The skill asks one focused audience question and does not label its rewrite final.
expectations: Recognizes that audience cannot be reliably inferred
Asks who the document is for or what decision they must make
May provide diagnosis but labels any rewrite partial

evals.prompt: Review this proposal for product managers: 'Our new cache reduced p99 latency by 60%, so we should enable it globally next week.' No benchmark or rollout evidence is attached.
evals.expected: The skill treats the metric as unverified, asks for confirmation or evidence, and does not polish it into certainty.
expectations: Labels the 60% claim as unverified rather than false
Requests the benchmark source or author confirmation
Identifies the unsupported jump from result to global rollout
Marks affected content as pending confirmation

evals.prompt: Review this memo for the service team: 'Reliability is important. Retries improve reliability. Therefore every request should retry five times.'
evals.expected: The skill diagnoses the reasoning gap itself and proposes a bounded, conditional formulation without asking the author whether the ideas are clear.
expectations: Finds missing conditions such as retryable failures, idempotency, and latency budget
Distinguishes the general opinion from an unsupported implementation rule
Offers a concrete improved structure or sentence
Asks the author only for unresolved facts, not for editorial diagnosis

evals.prompt: Review and refine this two-sentence reader-facing status memo for my team: 'The migration finished at 10:30 UTC. Error rates and latency remain within their normal ranges; continue monitoring until 12:30 UTC.'
evals.expected: The skill avoids rewriting a document that is already concise, clear, and audience-appropriate.
expectations: Returns few or no findings
Does not expand the note with generic background
Does not rewrite merely to appear useful
